answer.label: Written by Buffett; Munger influenced the idea
answer.sourceLine: The Berkshire Hathaway letter contains the sentence under Buffett’s signature, dated March 2, 1990. Immediately afterward Buffett says Charlie understood the principle early. That acknowledges Munger’s influence; the documented author of this sentence is Buffett.

source.heading: The source

author.name: Warren Buffett
author.heading: About Warren Buffett
author.bio: Warren Buffett is an American investor closely associated with Berkshire Hathaway. His shareholder letters explain business purchases and investing decisions in accessible language. He repeatedly acknowledged Charlie Munger’s influence on his preference for strong businesses over merely cheap ones.

context.heading: The setting behind the words
lead: Buffett is explaining why apparently cheap acquisitions can disappoint when the underlying business is weak. The surrounding section contrasts low purchase prices with durable earning power and acknowledges Charlie’s earlier understanding. The sentence belongs to Buffett’s signed shareholder letter even though the strategy reflects their partnership. Berkshire shareholder letter ↗
